report.code_assessment: The code follows the spec very closely: nearly every source file maps onto one or two scopes, uses their wording, and matches their behaviour down to labels, tooltips, ordering, and colours, and the comments often restate the spec's sentences. The few real departures are small. The divergence panel's build step shows a tick even when the build fails, and only mentions the failure in its notes. The palette labels Build as "Build Spec". The editor runs `piton format` when saving a Piton file. The hidden anchor gains a `mode` property. Sending a prompt with no project open shows an error notification. Where the code goes beyond the spec, it is mostly filling in concrete numbers (sizes, spring constants, timeouts, polling intervals), the exact CLI flags for the harness, git plumbing, and rendering workarounds for gpui-kit. There are also a few stale doc comments, such as the diff view's comment saying it sits beside the task view and the project directory's comment saying it lasts only for the session.
report.spec_assessment: The spec is broad and unusually precise. Most scopes pin down labels, tooltips, keyboard shortcuts, sizes, colours, order and edge cases. Nearly every behavioural scope has a clearly matching Rust module that was plainly written from it, often using the spec's own wording in comments and tests. Where the code drifts, the drift is small: a few labels differ, some things refresh by polling where the spec implies they react to changes, a few file extensions are missing, and shared components the spec treats as scopes of their own (the ranked selection list, the minimizable panel, the task table, the history list) are copied into each view or folded into bigger modules. The parts that say little on purpose are the index files that only re-export, the abstract lib anchors, the thin build-scope skill wrappers and the no-project scope, which leaves its wording to each place that uses it. Harness discovery and the exact claude flags are also left open.

well_defined.name: Divergence analysis
well_defined.why: The spec pins down the steps, the agent prompts, how results merge, the formulas for every measure, colour thresholds, tabs, report sections, and every tooltip, so the model and view are almost pure transcription.

well_defined.name: Chat input, hidden anchor and LSP
well_defined.why: Tab order, Chain behaviour, tint transitions, escaping rules, auto-imports, blanking for the draft, attachments, and completion triggers and ranking are all spelled out precisely.

well_defined.name: Ribbon and its tabs
well_defined.why: Each tab scope lists its groups, commands, icons, tooltips, primary flags, and disabled states, and the ChangeRibbon skill even dictates one code module per tab.

well_defined.name: File system browsers
well_defined.why: The shared FsBrowser scope and its folder and file variants define the navigation bar, keyboard shortcuts on both platforms, type-to-select, new-folder validation, and footer behaviour.

well_defined.name: New Project
well_defined.why: The layout, validation rules, templates, config generation (including anchor naming and adapters), git initialization, and the .gitignore contents are all specified.

well_defined.name: Scrollbar and task table
well_defined.why: Thumb geometry and colours, lock-to-bottom semantics, the pulse, measurement steadiness, badge kinds, streaming rows, and collapsed steps are described in detail.

well_defined.name: New project creation
well_defined.why: The field rules, the two-column layout, the templates, the exact piton.config.pi to write, the Git setup and the no-overwrite rules are all stated.

well_defined.name: Scrollbar
well_defined.why: It fixes the geometry, the thumb colours, measuring rows that aren't in view, lock-to-bottom behaviour and the timing and look of the lock pulse.

well_defined.name: Git panel and diff view
well_defined.why: The summary format, commit message assembly, pull merge rules, diff layouts, context lines, collapsing and navigation keys are all concrete.

well_defined.name: Chat input and hidden anchor
well_defined.why: It gives exact rules for escaping userPrompt, the attachedText format, mention triggers, tab cycling and the Chain tab's animation and colours.

less_defined.name: Visual metrics and animation tuning
less_defined.why: Sizes, paddings, max heights, spring stiffness and damping, dim levels, and slide durations are nearly all chosen by the implementation, with the spec only saying things like "quick" or "settles without bouncing".

less_defined.name: Harness and CLI invocation
less_defined.why: The spec says auto mode, stdin, appended system prompts, and carrying on conversations, but the exact claude flags (stream-json, fork-session, system-prompt-snapshot, haiku with low effort for notes) and the output parsing are left to the code.

less_defined.name: Git plumbing
less_defined.why: GitScope and GitPanelScope describe outcomes, but porcelain parsing, reading the committed file, trial merges with merge-tree, diff size caps, and polling intervals are the implementation's own choices.

less_defined.name: Main window panel orchestration
less_defined.why: The precedence of Esc across the palette, dialogs, lists, and panels, how focus is trapped and restored, and how Generate Skills opens are not described in MainWindowScope.

less_defined.name: Markdown rendering and link resolution
less_defined.why: The inline-code workaround, the markdown state cache thresholds, and resolving relative links by path suffix have no spec behind them beyond "links are clickable" and the scrollbar's steadiness requirements.

less_defined.name: Error wording and edge handling
less_defined.why: Many error, empty-state, and notification texts, and what happens with no project or unreadable config, are filled in by the code where the spec only says to "say why".

less_defined.name: Spec scaffolding (index files, lib anchors, build-scope skills)
less_defined.why: These files only re-export or declare abstract shapes and thin skill wrappers, so they say little about behaviour, and only the skill generator's file format traces back to them.

less_defined.name: Harness integration and catalog
less_defined.why: It names claude -p only as an example and says 'auto mode' without the flags. It doesn't say how user, project and plugin skills and agents are found, or what happens when the harness is missing.

less_defined.name: No-project state
less_defined.why: It deliberately leaves the wording to each use and doesn't say whether sending a prompt without a project should fail quietly or notify, which the code does.

less_defined.name: Project locations
less_defined.why: It defines the locations and the file-listing rules but no single owner. As a result the code walks files separately in the palette, divergence and rescope, each slightly differently.

less_defined.name: Prompt modes' colours
less_defined.why: Colours are given only as 'a subtle red', 'purple' and so on, with no values or contrast targets.
